Your bookmark manager is built, and I've switched from exploring to delivering the finished software.

**→ Open it here: http://maker:4000**

It starts empty — your own private library, ready for its first link (paste a web address at the top to begin).

**Verification report — in plain terms, everything we agreed on has been checked and passes:**

- **Saving** — paste an address (with or without `https://`), details fill in automatically, and you can edit everything; mistyped addresses are caught, and you can still save by hand when a page's details can't be read. ✓
- **Tags & notes** — add your own, with suggestions from tags you already use. ✓
- **Finding** — search across title, description, site, address, tags and notes; filter by clicking a tag; sort by newest, oldest, or title. ✓
- **Read later** — flag links into a focused list and clear them when read. ✓
- **Archiving** — tuck links away to keep the main list uncluttered, and restore anytime. ✓
- **Editing & no duplicates** — edit any bookmark (including its address); the app prevents duplicate links and sends you to the existing one instead, wherever it lives. ✓
- **Holds up** — welcoming when empty, tidy with very long text and many tags. ✓
- **Nothing gets lost** — your bookmarks are saved to durable storage, so they persist. ✓

Under the hood I ran **39 automated tests — 21 internal checks and 18 that replay each of the 12 agreed behaviors — and all pass.** The finished app was built fresh (not from the throwaway prototypes), and I've kept a record mapping each behavior to its code and tests for the future.

One honest note: automatically reading a page's details needs internet access to that page; if a page can't be reached, the app cleanly falls back to letting you fill in the details yourself — exactly the behavior we approved.

**Do you accept this software and agree to complete this cycle?** If anything doesn't behave the way we approved, tell me and I'll correct it within this cycle; anything genuinely new I'll note for a later round.
